PB-010 FINDING, CORRECTED BY PB-011 (do not 'fix' in the test layer): the UNDERLYING insight holds - some TS2339 in this project are union-narrowing artifacts of `strictNullChecks: false` inherited from the root tsconfig; TypeScript does not narrow boolean-discriminated unions (`{ok:true}|{ok:false}`) when strictNullChecks is off, and those tests already narrow correctly. But PB-010's MAGNITUDE WAS WRONG and its implication was backwards. PB-010 claimed '117 of the remaining 470 are TS2339 false positives ... TS2339 drops 227 -> 110 genuine'. That does not reproduce. PB-011 re-measured on 2026-07-21 with TypeScript 5.9.2 by re-running this exact project with --strictNullChecks: TS2339 goes 227 -> 156, a drop of 71 (about 15% of the 470-error backlog, not 25%).

PB-011 MEASUREMENT (the number that matters): enabling --strictNullChecks does NOT reduce this project's debt, it RAISES it - total errors go 470 -> 595 (+125, +27%). The TS2339 relief is more than cancelled by codes that only exist or expand under strictness: TS2322 49 -> 94, TS2345 33 -> 89, TS2352 74 -> 81, TS18048 26 -> 40, and newly appearing TS18047 (23), TS2571 (18), TS18049 (18), TS2454 (6), TS2783 (4), TS18046 (4), TS2698 (2), TS2739 (1). strictNullChecks is a debt-DISCLOSURE lever, not a debt-REDUCTION lever: it reveals ~125 real null/undefined hazards the current configuration hides. Turning it on is a deliberate, separately budgeted remediation programme, not a shortcut to a lower number. PB-011 changed NO strictness setting and no tsconfig.
CI fails if a count INCREASES. Lower a number (never raise it) as debt is genuinely fixed, in a dedicated reviewed commit.

PB-011: this scalar total is NO LONGER the whole gate. A count-only ratchet is defeated by fixing one error and introducing a different one - the total holds and the build stays green while new debt lands (exactly how PB-005/PB-008 put 4 errors into this baseline unattributed). scripts/typecheck-certification-fingerprints.json now carries a PER-ERROR IDENTITY baseline - (file, TS code, normalized message) with a count per bucket - and scripts/typecheck-certification.js FAILS on any net-new identity even when this total is unchanged. The two artifacts must be regenerated together; the guard fails if their totals disagree.

PB-011: the 4 PB-005/PB-008 errors are already absorbed inside the 470 and CANNOT be retroactively attributed - the count-only baseline recorded no identity for them, so there is nothing to diff them against. They are grandfathered as pre-existing debt. Attribution begins from this baseline forward.

PB-011: regenerate baselines ONLY via `npm run typecheck:certification:baseline`. It refuses to run under CI, refuses to RAISE a total, and refuses to absorb a net-new fingerprint unless --accept-new-debt is passed explicitly (which prints every absorbed fingerprint so it lands in the review record). Re-baselining is a governance act, never a build side effect.

Gaming this with blanket any / @ts-ignore / @ts-nocheck / excluding failing files is out of contract. The coverage assertion in scripts/typecheck-certification.js exists specifically so that dropping files from a project fails the check instead of lowering the count.
